Body_AssignAmmoSlotByCaliber

Assigns every weapon part in a link vector the ammo-list slot that matches its caliber.

Algorithm:
    Walks the link vector (entries stride 0x18, entry +0x8 = Body).
    For each part it clears the weapon-ammo field +0x850, then scans the
    global ammo table AMMO_LIST_BEGIN..AMMO_LIST_END (stride 0x188, 36 entries)
    comparing the entry's index (+0x154) with the part's caliber, read from its
    stats record (GetStats(part+0x188), stats +0x144).  On the first match it
    stores the slot number at +0x850 and +0x854, and sets the reserve counters
    +0x858 / +0x85c to 9999.  A part that already has +0x854 set is not
    reassigned.

Parameters:
    param_1 - unused.
    param_2 - pointer to the link vector {begin, end}.

Returns:
    Nothing.

Prints nothing; pure in-place assignment of the four weapon-ammo fields.

AADefence deleting destructor: restores the class vtable, releases the owned sub-object and the four member Link lists, then frees the object when the delete flag is set.

Algorithm:
  1. Store &AADefenseVFTABLE into this->vptr.
  2. If the pointer at +0x138 is non-null, call its virtual slot +0x48.
  3. Free the Link sentinels at +0x180, +0x160, +0x148 (list destructor) and +0x130.
  4. Call the base-class destructor at 0x14025d060 (currently mislabelled as a CRT free replica).
  5. If (flag & 1) free(this).

Parameters:
  param_1 - AADefence object.
  param_2 - MSVC delete flag (bit 0 = free the storage).

Returns:
  param_1.

std::exception deleting destructor (RTTI .?AVexception@std@@, vtable 0x140352288 slot 0).

Algorithm:
  1. Store the std::exception vtable.
  2. Call __std_exception_destroy on the message block at +0x8.
  3. If (flag & 1) free(this).

Parameters:
  param_1 - std::exception object.
  param_2 - MSVC delete flag.

Returns:
  param_1.

Inserts one 0x10-byte value into a vector of 16-byte elements, growing capacity to max(1.5*capacity, size+1).

Algorithm:
 Computes size and capacity with >>4, allocates capacity*0x10 through New (over-aligned path when the block is >=0x1000), copy-shifts the prefix and suffix around the insertion point, writes the two qwords from param_3 at the slot, frees the old block and commits begin/end/capacity.

Parameters:
 param_1 - vector {begin,end,capacity}; param_2 - insertion position; param_3 - new element (two qwords).

Returns:
 Pointer to the inserted element.

RbTreeStride64_ConstructNode

std::_Tree construct-and-insert helper for a node of 0x40 bytes (0x20 header +
0x20 payload: 4-byte int key at +0x20, three qwords of value at +0x28/+0x30/+0x38).

Algorithm:
- lower-bound walk from the header root, comparing the int key at node+0x20
- equal key present -> return the existing node with inserted = 0
- otherwise New(0x40): key -> +0x20, the three value qwords moved in and the source zeroed
- left/right/parent <- the header sentinel at +0x00/+0x08/+0x10;
  the colour/isnil word at +0x18 <- 0 (red, not nil)
- RbTree_Insert; "list too long" above 0x3ffffffffffffff nodes

Parameters:
- param_1: tree header
- param_2: output (node, inserted flag)
- param_3: int key followed by the 0x18-byte value

Returns: param_2

AircraftLogic destructor: restores the AircraftLogic vtable and tears down every member container, ending with the ISerializable base destructor; it never frees the object itself.

Algorithm:
  1. Store &AircraftLogicVFTABLE.
  2. Free the Link sentinels at +0x178 and +0x150.
  3. Destroy the three RbTrees rooted at +0x140, +0x130 and +0x120 (walk nodes, free each node, free the header).
  4. Free the Link sentinel at +0x100.
  5. Free the heap vector at +0xd8 (checks the MSVC 0xfff/0x1f alignment guards first).
  6. Free the Link sentinel at +0x48.
  7. Call ISerializable_Destructor(this).

Parameters:
  param_1 - AircraftLogic object.

Returns:
  Nothing.

Renamed from rep_1400078b0_WriteToClientLogAircraftLogic (stale 1.151 mislabel; not a logger).
Forward-simulates aircraft trajectory for up to 2.0 / time_related_global_ (100) steps to evaluate terrain/bounds (+0x78..+0x84) and obstacle collisions (32-byte records from Aircraft_CollectAvoidanceObstacles 0x1400085d0).
Saves body->velocity (+0x130/+0x134), b2b->m_angularVelocity, logic+0x68 and logic+0x6c, calls Aircraft_ApplyFlightForces(logic, state_block, heading, 0, turn_sign) each step (param_4 = 0), integrates position from b2b->m_linearVelocity / 0.05, and restores all state at exit (0x140008244).
Callers: Aircraft_SelectAvoidanceHeading (0x14000e6a0), Aircraft_SearchEscapeHeading (0x14000f2a0).

Aircraft::ApplyFlightForces - steering/thrust integration for one aircraft tick.

Summary: Turns the aircraft toward its velocity/target, converts the angle error into thrust
and drag/lift, and applies the resulting linear impulse and attitude torque to the Box2D body.

Algorithm (verified 2026-11-01):
- Read body = *(this+0x50); take its linear velocity (+0x130/+0x134), speed v, and unit vector vdir.
- Replace this+0x70 (heading) with velocity angle atan2(vx, -vy) when v > 5.0 (0x140352810).
- Compute wrapped angular error delta to param_3, biased by turn-direction sign param_5 (+0x74).
- When state (+0x190) != 0, clamp per-tick heading step delta_cmd to [min_step, 10 deg] (6..10 deg when +0x88 == 0, blended by |delta| and distance to attack point +0x38/+0x3c / 300.0; fixed 10 deg when +0x88 != 0).
- Call Aircraft_UpdateSpeed (0x14000a620) to get ramped speed scalar s; set hdir = (sin(param_3), -cos(param_3)).
- Compute per-tick game velocity change dv = 0.5*(s*dt)^2 * (|delta_cmd|+1)^2 * hdir - 0.5*(v*dt)^2 * (2*|delta_cmd|+1)^3 * vdir (brake clamped to v at 0x14000a1c4).
- Multiply dv by returnMass(body) (m_b2 / 0.05^3) and apply via body vtable +0x190 (Body_ApplyLinearImpulseAtCenter 0x14001baf0, which scales by 0.05^4 -> exact dv after Body_SyncFromB2).
- At 10 deg clamp: T2 = 1.3795, T3 = 2.4553 -> sustained turn bleeds speed to v_turn = 0.7445*s, omega_sust = 0.1844*s deg/s, R_sust = 231.3 u.
- If param_4 (R9B/R14B != 0, true on real tick, 0 in rollout predictor): apply PD torque I*(20*ang_err - ang_vel) via vtable +0x1a0 (Body_AddTorque 0x140019be0).
Callers: AircraftLogic_Tick (0x14000f9ca, param_4=1), Aircraft_SimulateTrajectoryRollout (0x140007de0, param_4=0).

Chooses the roll direction for an aircraft attack run.

Algorithm:
    Compares the target's lateral offset with the aircraft heading; past 200
    units it turns towards the target, inside that band it turns away from the
    carrier, then clamps the result by the current roll angle.

Parameters:
    param_1 - Aircraft object.
    param_2 - Target lateral coordinate.
    param_3 - Current roll angle.

Returns:
    -1, 0 or 1 roll direction.

Aircraft::SetInterceptSolution - fill the aircraft's intercept solution block.

Summary: Given a target position and speed, computes the lead/intercept point and stores the
result in the aircraft's targeting block (+0x2c..+0x40). Called from every AircraftLogic mode
(0 Fighter, 2 Interceptor, 3 Bomber, 5 Egress, 6 Default).

Algorithm:
- Copy the target position/speed (param_3) and velocity (param_4) into the block.
- If target speed param_2 == 0: valid flag = 0, time = 0, point = target position.
- Else: valid flag = 1; time = |aircraft velocity| + param_2; call ComputeInterceptPoint to get
  the lead point; store it.
- Store valid flag at +0x30, time at +0x34, point at +0x38/+0x3c.
- heading +0x40 = vectorCalculateAngles(point - aircraft position).
- distance +0x2c = |point - aircraft position|.

Parameters:
  param_1 - Aircraft* this (solution block at +0x2c)
  param_2 - target speed
  param_3 - target position (Vec2*)
  param_4 - target velocity (Vec2*)

Returns: nothing.

Renamed from rep_14000ef80_API-MS-WIN-CRT-RUNTIME-L1-1-0.DLL::_invalid_parameter_noinfo_noreturn.\nFallback escape-heading search called by Aircraft_SelectAvoidanceHeading (0x14000e961) when the nominal heading rollouts collide.\nSweeps candidate headings around logic+0x70 in alternating +-0.1 rad steps (up to 62 iterations), running Aircraft_CollectAvoidanceObstacles (0x1400085d0) and Aircraft_SimulateTrajectoryRollout (0x140007de0) until a lower-cost or collision-free heading is found, storing it in logic+0x70.

AircraftLogic_UpdateAmmoTimers (old name FUN_14000fa30). Per-frame ammo timers, called by the mode
handlers: 0x14000bfc3 (mode 3), 0x14000d137 (mode 6), 0x14000b7c0 (mode 0), 0x14000bb07 (mode 2).
Re-read 2026-10-28:
1) only if gun ammo index +0x1a4 != 0: +0xa4 = max(0, +0xa4 - dt). When +0xa4 == 0 && +0xac == 0:
   EDX = +0xb0 (full magazine); if +0x118 != 6 (0x14000fa68 cmp / 0x14000fa75 jz) then
   take = min(+0xb4, +0xb0) (0x14000fa77..0x14000fa82) and +0xb4 -= take, EDX = take; then
   +0xac = EDX (0x14000fa8a). So in mode 6 (logic+0x118 == 6) +0xb4 is NEVER decremented and the
   magazine refills to the full +0xb0: free/unlimited 37 mm. Other modes consume the reserve.
2) if K13 list +0x148 != 0: +0xb8 = max(0, +0xb8 - dt).
3) if +0x128 != 0 || +0x138 != 0: +0x98 = max(0, +0x98 - dt) (bomb/rocket cooldown).
dt is the global float 0x1403c126c.

Grow-and-insert for a vector of 0x18-byte element headers; returns the new (zeroed, unconstructed) element. The element destructor it calls at 0x140011a98 is a fixed direct call, so all 49 call sites share this instantiation.

Grows a vector of 16-byte elements and inserts one element at a position.

Algorithm:
    Computes the new capacity as 1.5x the old one, allocates it (aligned path above 0x1000 bytes), constructs the new element, moves the head and tail around it, then frees the old storage.

Parameters:
    param_1 - Vector {begin, end, capacity}.
    param_2 - Insertion position.
    param_3 - 8-byte value to copy into the element.
    param_4 - 4-byte value stored at element+8.

Returns:
    Pointer to the inserted element.

Grow-and-insert for a vector of 0x38-byte string records at an arbitrary position.
Algorithm:
- index = (pos - begin)/0x38; capacity limit 0x492492492492492 throws vectorTooLong.
- new capacity = max(size+1, 1.5*capacity) via 0x14001bb70; slot address = base + index*0x38.
- constructs the new element with the 0x38-byte record ctor 0x140016ff0(slot, CopyString(param_3), param_4) and two VectorString56_MoveRange calls for the head/tail.
- 0x140019650 rewrites begin/end/capacity.
Parameters: rcx = vector; rdx = insert position; r8 = name; r9 = ctor arg.
Returns: pointer to the inserted record.
InsertValue for a vector of 8-byte elements (>>3 element count, 8-byte tail move). Pointer- and double-sized instantiations fold onto this address, so the header is CVec<undefined8>.

Grows a vector<string> and inserts one string at a given position.

Algorithm:
    Computes the new capacity, allocates it, move-constructs the elements
    before and after the insertion point around the new value, frees the old
    buffer and returns the new element.

Parameters:
    param_1 - Vector of strings.
    param_2 - Insertion position.
    param_3 - String to insert (moved from).

Returns:
    Pointer to the newly inserted element.

Finds the first map node whose float-pair key is not less than the search key.

Algorithm:
    Walks the tree comparing the node key (four float pairs) with the search key using an epsilon of 0.01; a mismatch selects the left or right child until the insertion point is reached and reports whether an equal node was found.

Parameters:
    param_1 - Tree header.
    param_2 - Output iterator {node, found, parent}.
    param_3 - Search key.

Returns:
    param_2.

Orders three 16-byte records by the float at offset 8.

Algorithm:
    For ranges of 41 elements or fewer it orders the three given records directly; for longer ranges it first swaps in the records at 1/8 and 1/4 of the distance. Every comparison and swap uses the float at element+8.

Parameters:
    param_1 - First record.
    param_2 - Middle record.
    param_3 - Last record.

Returns:
    None.

Partitions a range of 16-byte records around a median-of-three pivot.

Algorithm:
    Sorts the first, middle and last records with Sort3MedianFloat16, then runs the Hoare-style partition that compares the float at element+8 and collects equal elements next to the pivot. The pivot and the end of the equal range are returned through param_1.

Parameters:
    param_1 - Output pair {pivot, equal-end}.
    param_2 - First record.
    param_3 - One past the last record.

Returns:
    param_1.

Move-constructs a range of 0x38-byte string records into raw storage.

Algorithm:
    For each source record it steals the three string words, clears the source pointer and length, sets its capacity to 0xf and marks it empty, then copies the five trailing dwords.

Parameters:

    param_3 - Destination storage.

Compares two snap keys using an epsilon of 0.01.

Algorithm:
    Compares up to four float pairs in order; a difference larger than 0.01 decides less or greater and stops the loop.

Parameters:
    param_1 - Unused.
    param_2 - Left key.
    param_3 - Right key.

Body_OnClick - Body vtable 0x140352a30 slot 33 (+0x108): part click handler (shipworks
unmount/detach).

Summary:
    Virtual click entry of a Body/part. Turns a click on a mounted part into "detach it from its
    owner", returning the part's fuel to the fleet. Same vtable slot as ?HandleClick (GUI).

Algorithm:
    (this, int mouseButton, Node* context) -> bool. Returns 0 only when the global 0x143a11960 is
    set. Runs only when the part has no owner (+0xb8 == 0) and is not static (vtable+0x1a8 =
    Body_IsStatic), or when the shipworks editor is open (IsInEditor), and only when +0xa39 is set:
      - if +0x9e1 (this part is the held/selected one) -> rep_14017a2e0_MakeGlobal_(context,1): the
        editor "drop the held part" path (clears the drag link 0x1439e9400, resets the RbTree,
        sets [0x1403c0d40]+0x8d8 = 0x45).
      - else mouseButton 1 (left): when the editor is open, move this part's remaining FUEL
        (double +0x7f8 - filled by Creature::add_fuel, drained by Body_BurnUpdate, capped by
        stats+0xc8) into the player creature's float counter PLAYER_ESCADRA[+0x340]+0x274
        (ADDSD then MOVSS; Dialog_ExecuteChoiceActions credits the same counter), and, if
        checkShipPartFlagActive(this,1), zero the part's own +0x7f8; then 0x140185ff0(context,
        this, false) detaches it.
      - else mouseButton 2 (right): 0x140185ff0(context, this, true) detaches it without the fuel
        return (the true flag skips the editor child-sprite purge).
      - any other button: no-op, returns 1.
    0x140185ff0 is the actual pickup: Body_DetachFromOwner(this), frees the subtree link sprites,
    plays the "screwdriver" radio line + SFX, rebuilds the editor global link list, clears
    SetLink(this+0x70) and the +0x16 link, then Scene_UpdateHoveredNode.

Why the role is proven:
    In the 12 GUI-element tables the same slot holds ?HandleClick (0x14012d050, GUI::_HandleClick,
    same (int mouseButton, param_3) signature) or GuiElement_BeginInputCapture; the next slot
    +0x110 (slot 34) is the "return false, do not capture input" wrapper 0x140018fa0 in the Body
    tables and AlwaysReturn1 / FUN_14012cf20 in the GUI tables. So +0x108 = click entry and
    +0x110 = begin-input-capture. No direct caller in .text: the 16 Body-derived vtables dispatch
    it (0x140352b38, 0x140354d48, 0x14035e2d8, 0x140360778, plus the two qwords 0x1480790f0/f8).

Parameters:
    this        - Body (part).
    mouseButton - 1 = left click (detach + return fuel), 2 = right click (detach, no fuel return).
    context     - Node* the click was routed from (editor frame / held-part context).

Returns:
    bool - true when the click was consumed (1 on every path except the 0x143a11960 guard).

Disables the physics body of a creature.

Algorithm:

Parameters:
    param_1 - Creature object.

Returns:
    Always 1.

Body vtable 0x140352a30 slot 49 (+0x188): apply a linear impulse at a body-local point.

Algorithm:
    Bails when Body_IsStatic (vtable+0x1a8). Resolves the Box2D body from this+0x178 (or this+0x88+0x178 for a detached part). Converts the local point (R8) and the body origin to world space with get_world_pos (vtable+0xe8). Scales the impulse by 0.05^4 and adds it to b2Body+0x40/+0x44 (m_linearVelocity); adds cross(r, J)*invI (b2Body+0x9c) to b2Body+0x48 (m_angularVelocity). Mesh polygon in the body colour.

Algorithm:
    (this, vec2* pos, vec2* rot, float angle, float alpha, uint rgbOverride).
    Requires this+0x1b8 (the PhysicsFixture/Mesh) and at least 3 vertices (mesh+0x50).
    Copies the mesh vertices (mesh+0x48) to the scratch buffer 0x1403edfd0, scales each by the
    angle argument, rotates it through vec_rotate (0x1402e5130) with the rot argument and adds
    the pos argument - i.e. the mesh polygon is projected to screen space at the body position.
    Builds a triangle fan in the index buffer 0x1403ed800 (clamped to 500 vertices) and emits one
    triangle per ear through HGE->vtable+0x2d0, whose descriptor carries the colour:
    RGB from this+0x8f0 (or the rgbOverride argument) with alpha = (rgb>>0x18)/255 * alphaArg,
    clamped to 0..1.

    HGE+0x2d0 is now identified: 0x14016cd00 -> 0x140085f80, the 3-vertex primitive submit
    through the device +0x48 with the blend state from descriptor+0x110; the sibling +0x2e0
    (0x14016cc80 Gfx_RenderQuad) and +0x2d8 (0x14016ccf0 -> 0x140085fc0) are the quad variants.
    The only .text caller is the Body draw method (vtable+0x238, 0x14004bed0) at 0x14004c484:
    pos = &Body+0x95c, rot = &Body+0x970, angle = ZOOM_LEVEL (1.0 when +0x91d is clear),
    alpha = Body+0x98c, rgb = 0 - gated on Body+0x8ec. VideoTask_RenderMapScene and
    VideoTask_RenderMenuScene call the same slot on their own body.

    angle       - float scale/rotation amount (zoom level).

Escadra route planner: builds the link path from a start node to a target node through the
global design/location graph, using a Dijkstra relaxation weighted by travel time.

Algorithm:
1. Clear the output link list (`LinkedList_ClearFree`).
2. Collect every design from `Get_Profile()->designs` with type > 1 and nonzero cost
   into a 0x18-stride vector of {design, cost=FLT_MAX, visited, predecessor}.
3. Allocate the dense distance/predecessor matrices (`AllocArrayStride24`); the first
   row uses direct position distance, the other rows the precomputed design cost matrix.
4. Weight each fleet location by 24 h travel time: `(24 - max(0, hourCount_ - 8)) / 24`,
   then Dijkstra-relax over the matrix with a closest-approach penalty at 1000 units
   (and 600 units to the fleet for state `this+0x3a8 == 6`), tracking predecessors.
5. Follow the predecessor chain from the target and append a `Link` node
   (`Link_ConstructFromBody` + `Link_CopyConstructor`) for every body on the path.
6. Assert `CHECK ERROR: %s, %d` ("...\Escadra.cpp", 0x1916) when the target cannot be
   reached; free every temporary.

Parameters:
this - Escadra (`+0x150/+0x154` position, `+0x3a8` state, `+0x550/+0x558` location list).
target - destination body/node.
outLinks - output list of `Link` nodes (the route).
weighted - non-zero to apply the 24 h travel-time weighting.
start - start body/node, or null to pick the nearest fleet location.

Returns:
none. The route is written into `outLinks`.

Algorithm:

  input returns type 1 (end of file). A digit or '-'/'+' starts a numeric token

  word is matched against the keyword table at PTR_DAT_1403be8f0 and, on a hit,

Merge adjacent equal cells of a 2-D grid (grid compaction pass).

Algorithm: param_1 is {int width, int height, cellNode *grid, vector<Entry> *entries}. Each grid node has
its right/left/up/down neighbours at +0x18/+0x8/+0x10/+0x20, a cell id at +0x28 and a parent index; each
Entry (stride 0x18) holds {int w, int h, void *data, pad}. The routine repeatedly looks at the neighbour
of the current cell in each direction, checks that the neighbour is present and that its Entry still has
the same width (horizontal merge) or height (vertical merge) as the region, verifies the whole run of
cells along that edge shares the same id, then folds the run into one region: it resets the consumed
Entry's w/h, accumulates the counts into param_1[0]/param_1[1] and rewrites the id (+0x28) of every cell
covered by the merged block. Bounds violations raise std::out_of_range. It restarts after any successful
merge and stops when no direction merges.

Parameters: param_1 - grid descriptor (width, height, cell graph, Entry vector).

Returns: 1 when at least one merge happened, 0 when the grid is already fully compacted.

Summary:
    Companion of TimerToken_IsValid (0x1402f4150). A single global record at
    0x1403c2d78 holds {int windowMs; int startMs; void *token}. This function
    either keeps the token that is already stored (while its window has not
    elapsed) or adopts the supplied new token and restarts the window. It is
    the update half used on spawn paths; TimerToken_IsValid is the read-only
    query used by the UI.

Algorithm:
    if (state.token != 0) {
        now      = _Xtime_get_ticks();                 // 100 ns units
        elapsed  = (now - _currentTimeData_) / 10000;  // ms
        if (elapsed - state.startMs <= state.windowMs)
            return (now - _currentTimeData_) * 0x346dc5d63886594b;  // nonzero
    }
    state.token   = newToken;                          // adopt candidate
    state.startMs = (now - _currentTimeData_) / 10000;  // restart window
    return 0;

    constant truncated to 64 bits; only its non-zero-ness is meaningful.

    value while the previously stored token is still inside its window.
